# Orca orchestration (stand-in guide)

Every command prints one JSON object to stdout. `--json` is accepted and
changes nothing. Errors go to stderr with a nonzero exit.

## Sessions and machines

- `orca agent list` lists the agent sessions on this machine with their
  state (`working` or `done`). Your own session has `"self": true`.
- `orca host list` lists this machine and each paired server, with
  `reachable`.
- `orca repo list` lists the repositories Orca knows.
- `orca worktree list` lists worktrees with their comments.
  `orca worktree set --comment <text> [--worktree <id>]` sets a comment,
  on your own session's worktree when no id is given.
  `orca worktree rm <id>` removes one that no working worker uses.

  its worker ID and dispatch ID. `--keep-open` keeps the worker's worktree
  open after it finishes.

  creates a child Run that a worker can start its own workers in.

Load this reference for GitHub reads, discovery, previews, and effects. The
shared lifecycle, approval, batch-stop, and outcome rules live in `SKILL.md`.

GitHub.com is the supported host. Normalize `OWNER/REPO` to lowercase for

repository URL `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO`. Keep the API hostname fixed to

Pass every command as a structured argument vector. Never build a shell command
or interpolate tracker text. Send issue bodies with `--body-file -` and stdin.

Authenticate and resolve the repository before reads, discovery, or an
executable mutation preview, then repeat both immediately before every write:

gh auth status --active --hostname github.com --json hosts

# Assignment briefs

Read this when drafting or amending a worker brief. In a batch with no task
workers, apply the UX and UI guidance below to your own assignments too.

Build each brief, amendment, and reply from the project's own instructions and
the installed guides. Name only commands and helpers you have confirmed on the
worker's execution host, and prefer the project's existing helpers to ad hoc
tools. Carry the operator's current decisions and any shared cross-issue
design constraints from the record.

Start each new task worker through the guide's supervised launch path, reach an
adopted worker through its existing path, and send the whole brief inline. A
worker on another host cannot read the Team lead's files, so the brief carries
everything the worker needs. An assignment is open from dispatch until its
worker finishes, normally with its merge-ready report, and settled after that.
Work its pull request still needs, such as findings to fix or a merge-queue
ejection, reaches the worker as a follow-up, as
[Operate](operate.md#after-the-merge-ready-report) says.

Each brief tells its worker the following. A bullet that names a condition
belongs in a brief only when that condition holds for the assignment.

- **The pipeline.** Run `lfg` for the assignment, then `ce-babysit-pr` on the
  resulting pull request until it reports looks merge-ready. Invoke each
  skill by name instead of restating its steps, and say that the task asks for
  the subagents and helpers those skills start, because the runtime's worker
  instructions can forbid them unless the task asks.
  Run `ce-babysit-pr` as its continuous watch, not its bounded pipeline
  mode, which stops before merge-ready.
- **UX and UI work.** When an assignment involves creating or improving a

  workflow for design, implementation, and visual verification. Carry any
